mainTopic: Moving ציצית between garments, קלא אילן on an all-תכלת טלית, and the required number and length of ציצית strings
overview: The amud continues the discussion of moving ציצית from one garment to another. Two attempts to prove that this is always allowed are pushed back. In the end, a dispute between רב (forbids) and שמואל (permits) is cited, along with two parallel disputes: lighting from one נר to another, and following רבי שמעון on dragging on שבת. אביי reports that רבה, who usually followed רב, followed שמואל in all three, so moving ציצית is allowed in practice. In between, ברייתות discuss a טלית made entirely of תכלת and when strings of קלא אילן are פסול, and רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the difference as four strings versus eight. Stories follow of how sages protected their ציצית when garments went to the launderer. A new ברייתא then gives בית שמאי's and בית הלל's numbers for how many strings are used and how long they hang, and רב פפא rules four strings, within three fingerbreadths of the edge, hanging four. The גמרא challenges this with a ברייתא saying ציצית have no measure, and it begins its answer at the end of the amud.

steps.title: The condition: the strings must not be broken
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא from the previous lines ends with a condition: moving the strings is allowed only if they are not broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as the strings are not broken.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last words of a ברייתא that allows moving ציצית strings to another garment. This sets up the גמרא's next question about what we can learn from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a permission, but only on one condition: the strings must still be whole. The גמרא now wants to know how broad that permission really is.

keyTerms.meaning: provided that, only on condition that
broken, cut off

phrases.english: Provided that it is not broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the ברייתא quoted just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moving ציצית strings to another garment is allowed only if the strings are not broken.

steps.title: Can we learn that strings may always be moved to another garment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to learn from the ברייתא a general rule: ציצית may be untied from one garment and put on another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we learn from this that one may untie ציצית from one garment and put them on another garment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to pull a general rule out of the ברייתא: strings may always be moved from garment to garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allowed moving strings that are not broken. The גמרא asks whether this means it is always fine to take strings off a good garment and move them, which is a much broader rule.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we learn from it? (an attempt to draw a rule from a source)
one may untie ציצית from one garment and move them to another

phrases.english: Should you learn from it
that one may untie from garment to garment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to draw a general rule from the ברייתא's permission.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one may always move ציצית from one garment to another.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that allows moving strings as long as they are not broken.

steps.title: Maybe only when the first garment is worn out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: maybe the ברייתא only allows moving the strings when the first garment has worn out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is only when the first garment has worn out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The ברייתא might be talking only about a garment that is already worn out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the old garment is worn out, it will not be used anyway, so moving its strings takes nothing away from it. That says nothing about taking strings off a garment that is still good, so the general rule is not proven.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps (opens a pushback on a proof)
worn out

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove that strings may always be moved. It may only allow it when the first garment is worn out.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is if it wore out.
phrases.notes: He means the first garment wore out and can no longer be worn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 2 by limiting the ברייתא to a narrower case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not rule that moving strings is forbidden.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may refer only to a worn-out garment, so it cannot teach a rule about garments that are still good.

steps.title: A טלית entirely of תכלת: any color except קלא אילן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a טלית made entirely of תכלת may get strings of any color except קלא אילן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: for a טלית that is entirely תכלת, strings of every color satisfy its obligation, except קלא אילן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a טלית dyed fully with תכלת: its non-תכלת strings may be any color except קלא אילן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קלא אילן is a cheap plant dye that looks just like real תכלת. The ברייתא's wording sounds like a strict rule: קלא אילן does not work at all, even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: a cloak or four-cornered garment
sky-blue wool dye required for ציצית
colors, dyed strings
exempt, meaning they satisfy the garment's ציצית obligation
indigo, a plant dye that looks like תכלת

steps.confusionAlert: "Exempt" here does not mean the garment needs no ציצית. It means these strings satisfy the obligation.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A cloak that is entirely sky-blue —
all kinds of colors exempt it,
except for indigo.
phrases.notes: קלא אילן looks exactly like תכלת but is not the real thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: which colors may be used for a טלית made entirely of תכלת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a טלית entirely of תכלת, any color of string works except קלא אילן.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says קלא אילן is כשר after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 4 with a ברייתא that says one should not use קלא אילן, but if one did, the ציצית are כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: a טלית is exempted only by strings of its own kind. For a טלית that is entirely תכלת, one brings תכלת and something else and attaches them. He should not bring קלא אילן, but if he did, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that seems to clash with the first one about קלא אילן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא implied that קלא אילן does not work at all. This ברייתא agrees you should not use it at the start, but says that once done, the ציצית are כשר. So the two ברייתות seem to disagree about the after-the-fact case.

keyTerms.meaning: its own kind, meaning strings matching the garment
something else, here a string of another color
hangs, attaches
valid, fit

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: טַלִּית אֵין פּוֹטֵר בָּהּ אֶלָּא מִינָהּ.
phrases.english: A cloak — only its own kind exempts it.
phrases.notes: The plain strings should match the garment's own color.

phrases.english: A cloak that is entirely sky-blue —

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא תְּכֵלֶת וְדָבָר אַחֵר וְתוֹלֶה בָּהּ,
phrases.english: he brings sky-blue and something else and attaches them to it,
but indigo he should not bring,
and if he brought it — it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the ברייתא of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 4 that קלא אילן does not work on a טלית entirely of תכלת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 4 implies קלא אילן is פסול even after the fact, while this ברייתא says that after the fact it is כשר.

steps.title: Four strings versus eight strings
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that one ברייתא speaks of a טלית with four strings and the other of a טלית with eight strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: it is not a contradiction. One ברייתא speaks of a טלית with four strings, the other of a טלית with eight strings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק resolves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is about a different number of strings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With four strings (two תכלת, two קלא אילן), the ציצית are כשר after the fact. That is the ברייתא of step 5. With eight strings (four and four), they are פסול, as in step 4. The common explanation is that four strings of קלא אילן could be taken off and used as a full set of 'תכלת' on another garment.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult; the contradiction is resolved
here... here; each source refers to a different case
strings

steps.whatToRemember: קלא אילן on a טלית entirely of תכלת is never allowed at the start. After the fact it is כשר with four strings but פסול with eight strings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic way the גמרא resolves a contradiction: it splits the cases, so both ברייתות stay true, each in its own situation.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is not difficult:
here it is a cloak with four strings,
phrases.notes: This is the case where it is כשר after the fact, the ברייתא of step 5.

phrases.english: there it is a cloak with eight strings.
phrases.notes: This is the case where it is פסול, the ברייתא of step 4.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ברייתא refers to a different number of strings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to disagree about whether קלא אילן is כשר after the fact.
steps.terutzMaskana: With four strings it is כשר after the fact. With eight strings it is פסול.

steps.title: Does this prove ציצית may be moved to another garment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the concern in the answer of step 6 proves ציצית may be untied from one garment and tied onto another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we learn from this that one may untie ציצית from one garment and put them on another?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at the answer in step 6 and asks whether it proves that moving ציצית between garments is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about using קלא אילן on an all-תכלת garment assumes the strings might later be moved to a different garment. If חז"ל worried about that happening, maybe that means moving strings is allowed in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: Can we learn from it? (a suggested conclusion)
One may untie
From one garment to another garment

phrases.english: Can you learn from this
that one may untie ציצית from one garment to another garment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule out of the answer given in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The general rule that ציצית may be moved from one garment to another
steps.raayaSupportSource: The concern behind the answer of רב נחמן בר יצחק, which assumes strings may be transferred

steps.title: Maybe the concern is only for someone who moved them anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the concern may only cover a case where someone went ahead and moved the strings, not a case where it was allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the worry is only about a case where he did it anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worrying about what might happen after someone moves the strings does not mean it is allowed to move them. Maybe it is not allowed at the start, but חז"ל still had to plan for a person who did it anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
That if he did it (after the fact)
After the fact, as opposed to permitted from the start

steps.confusionAlert: Protecting against what happens after someone does an action is not the same as permitting the action. This proof fails, but the question itself is decided in step 12.

phrases.english: Perhaps it means: in case he did it.
phrases.notes: He means: moving the strings may be forbidden from the start, but if someone did it anyway, we still worry about the result.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from step 7 only. No rule is decided either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Worrying about a possible action after the fact does not show that the action is allowed from the start.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about moving ציצית
steps.stepSummary: An explicit dispute: רב says ציצית may not be moved from garment to garment, and שמואל says they may.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב says one may not untie ציצית from one garment to put on another. שמואל says one may.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the proofs did not settle the question, the גמרא now cites a direct dispute between אמוראים on this exact question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question from steps 2 and 7 turns out to be a real argument. רב forbids moving the strings and שמואל permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not untie
A dispute
The sages of the גמרא era

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the direct statement of the question the whole section has been circling.

phrases.english: It was stated: רב says:
One may not untie ציצית from one garment to another garment,
and שמואל says: One may untie them from one garment to another garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof is rejected, the גמרא cites an explicit dispute on the same question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב forbids moving ציצית from one garment to another. שמואל permits it.

steps.title: A parallel dispute about lighting from one lamp to another
steps.stepSummary: רב says one may not light from one נר to another. שמואל says one may.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says one may not light from one lamp to another lamp. שמואל says one may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists a second dispute between רב and שמואל that follows the same pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again רב is strict and שמואל is lenient. The two topics are placed side by side because the structure of the disagreement is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: One may light
Lamp, candle
From one lamp to another

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין מִנֵּר לְנֵר,
phrases.english: רב says: One may not light from one lamp to another lamp,
phrases.notes: This is about חנוכה lamps, using one lit lamp to light another.

phrases.english: and שמואל says: One may light from one lamp to another lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין מִנֵּר לְנֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second רב/שמואל dispute with the same strict/lenient pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב forbids lighting from one lamp to another. שמואל permits it.

steps.title: A parallel dispute about following רבי שמעון on dragging
steps.stepSummary: רב says the הלכה is not like רבי שמעון regarding גרירה (dragging on שבת). שמואל says it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון about dragging. שמואל says the הלכה does follow רבי שמעון about dragging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third dispute between רב and שמואל, completing a set of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון allows dragging an object on שבת even though a groove might form, because the person does not intend to make one. רב does not rule like him and שמואל does, so again רב is strict and שמואל is lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows
Dragging an object along the ground
An unintended result of an action

steps.whatToRemember: Three disputes follow the same pattern: moving ציצית between garments, lighting from one נר to another, and גרירה like רבי שמעון. In all three, רב is strict and שמואל is lenient.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּגְרִירָה,
phrases.english: רב says: The הלכה is not like רבי שמעון regarding dragging,
phrases.notes: This is about dragging something like a bench on שבת, where a groove might form in the ground without the person meaning to make one.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּגְרִירָה.
phrases.english: and שמואל says: The הלכה is like רבי שמעון regarding dragging.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּגְרִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third רב/שמואל dispute with the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב does not rule like רבי שמעון on גרירה. שמואל does.

steps.title: רבה followed שמואל in these three rulings
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבה usually followed רב, but in the three disputes just quoted he followed שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In all matters, the Master (רבה) acted like רב, except in these three, where he acted like שמואל: one may move ציצית from one garment to another, one may light from one lamp to another, and the הלכה follows רבי שמעון about dragging.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells us how his teacher רבה actually ruled in the three disputes between רב and שמואל from steps 9-11. In all three he followed שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9-11 only listed the disputes. This step gives the practical ruling. Because רבה normally followed רב, the fact that he broke from רב here tells us that in these three cases the practice follows שמואל, including moving ציצית from garment to garment.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master', a respectful way of referring to one's teacher. Here it means רבה.
Except for
One may untie ציצית from one garment and tie them onto another
One may light one lamp from another lamp
Dragging an object along the ground on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: In practice (as רבה ruled), one may move ציצית from one garment to another, following שמואל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the question raised in steps 2 and 7 and argued by רב and שמואל in step 9: may ציצית be moved from one garment to another?

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In all matters, the Master acted like Rav,
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is רבה, אביי's teacher, who raised him.

phrases.english: except for these three, where he acted like Shmuel:
one may untie [ציצית] from garment to garment,
and one may light from lamp to lamp,
and the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon regarding dragging.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כֹּל מִילֵּי דְּמָר עָבֵיד כְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling for the three רב/שמואל disputes listed in steps 9-11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה followed שמואל in all three cases: moving ציצית from garment to garment is allowed, lighting from lamp to lamp is allowed, and dragging follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: What רבי שמעון said about dragging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that is the source of רבי שמעון's view on dragging furniture on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי שמעון says a person may drag a bed, chair, or bench, as long as he does not intend to make a groove in the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which ruling of רבי שמעון is meant by 'dragging' by quoting his words from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that if a person does not intend to cause a forbidden result, and that result is not certain to happen, the action is not forbidden. So dragging furniture is allowed as long as he is not trying to dig a groove, even though a groove might form.

keyTerms.meaning: Drags
Bench
A groove or furrow in the ground
As long as he does not intend

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
A person may drag a bed, a chair, or a bench,
as long as he does not intend to make a groove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the third item in אביי's list, 'dragging'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dragging furniture on שבת is allowed if one does not intend to make a groove.

steps.title: How three אמוראים protected their ציצית during washing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells how רב יהודה, רב חנינא and רבינא handled their ציצית when their garments went to be washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה gave his garment to the launderer as it was. רב חנינא tied his ציצית into a bundle. רבינא sewed a cover over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells three short stories about what different sages did with garments that had ציצית when they were sent to be washed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה was not worried and sent the garment as it was. רב חנינא tied the strings into a bundle, and רבינא sewed them in, to protect them while the garment was washed. The three show a range from no worry to more and more care.

keyTerms.meaning: A launderer, someone who washes clothes
A bundle (the strings tied together)
Sewing, stitching

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda would give it to the launderer,
phrases.notes: 'It' is his garment with the ציצית still on it.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥanina would make it into a bundle,
Ravina would sew them in with stitching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds practical stories about the worry, raised in steps 6-8, that strings could come loose or be switched (for example with קלא אילן). The sages differed on how much to guard against this while their garments were washed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sages treated ציצית on a garment being washed differently: some did not worry, and others bundled or sewed the strings to protect them.

steps.title: How many strings go into ציצית
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: בית שמאי say four strings are placed in the garment, and בית הלל say three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: How many strings does one put in? בית שמאי say four, and בית הלל say three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about how many strings are put into each corner. בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about moving ציצית and protecting them. Now it turns to how ציצית are made: the number of strings put through the hole in the corner. בית שמאי require four strings and בית הלל require three.

keyTerms.meaning: Strings, threads
Places, puts in

steps.confusionAlert: The number here counts the strings put through the hole. Each one is folded over, so twice as many ends hang down.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
How many strings does one put in?
Beit Shammai say: four,
and Beit Hillel say: three.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כַּמָּה חוּטִין הוּא נוֹתֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the number of strings in ציצית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: four strings are put in. בית הלל: three strings are put in.

steps.title: How long must the hanging strings be?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. בית שמאי say the strings must hang four fingerbreadths and בית הלל say three, where each fingerbreadth is a quarter of an average person's טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How long should the strings hang down? בית שמאי say: four fingerbreadths. בית הלל say: three. Each of בית הלל's three is one quarter of an ordinary person's handbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going. Now it asks how long the loose strings must hang below the knots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 was about how many strings are used. This step adds a second dispute, about the length of the hanging part. It also defines the unit: each fingerbreadth is one fourth of a normal person's טפח, so the measurement is not based on someone with unusually large or small hands.

keyTerms.meaning: The part of the strings that hangs loose below the knots and windings
A handbreadth, a standard measurement made up of four fingerbreadths
Of any ordinary person, meaning an average-sized hand

phrases.english: And how much should be hanging down?
phrases.notes: משולשת here means the loose part of the strings that hangs below the knots and windings.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: four (fingerbreadths),
and Beit Hillel say: three.
And the three that Beit Hillel say

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת מֵאַרְבַּע בְּטֶפַח שֶׁל כׇּל אָדָם.
phrases.english: are each one of the four in the handbreadth of any ordinary person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 15 and moves from the number of strings to their hanging length.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hanging length: בית שמאי say four fingerbreadths and בית הלל say three, each a quarter of an average טפח.

steps.title: Measuring a Torah handbreadth with different fingers
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that a Torah טפח equals four thumb-widths, six little-finger widths, or five middle-finger widths.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The Torah's handbreadth is four thumbs wide, six little fingers wide, or five middle fingers wide.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a side note to make the measurement concrete. He explains how many fingers make up one טפח, depending on which finger you measure with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke of a fingerbreadth as one quarter of a טפח. רב פפא shows that this only works out exactly when you measure with the thumb. Narrower fingers need more widths to fill the same טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: The handbreadth used for Torah measurements
Thumb
The little finger, literally the small one
The middle finger, literally the third one

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The handbreadth of the Torah
is four when measured by the thumb,
six by the little finger,
five by the third finger.
phrases.notes: The third finger counted from the edge of the hand is the middle finger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the unit of measurement mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Torah טפח = 4 thumbs = 6 little fingers = 5 middle fingers.

steps.title: רב הונא and רב יהודה give their numbers for ציצית
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says four strings, attached within four fingerbreadths of the edge, hanging four. רב יהודה says three strings, within three, hanging three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: four strings, placed within four fingerbreadths of the edge, hanging down four. רב יהודה says: three strings, placed within three fingerbreadths, hanging down three.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים each give a full rule for making ציצית. Each one gives three numbers: how many strings, how far from the edge, and how long they hang.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's numbers match the side of בית שמאי in the ברייתא: four strings and four fingerbreadths hanging. רב יהודה's numbers match בית הלל: three and three. The new detail here is how far from the edge of the garment the strings are attached.

keyTerms.meaning: Within, here meaning within a certain distance from the edge of the garment
Four strings placed within four fingerbreadths of the edge

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אַרְבָּעָה בְּתוֹךְ אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: Rav Huna says: four strings within four fingerbreadths,
phrases.notes: "Within four" means the hole for the strings is no more than four fingerbreadths from the edge of the garment.

phrases.english: and hanging down four.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: שְׁלֹשָׁה בְּתוֹךְ שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda says: three strings within three fingerbreadths,
hanging down three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אַרְבָּעָה בְּתוֹךְ אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא to the אמוראים, who each give a practical set of measurements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: 4 strings, within 4, hanging 4. רב יהודה: 3 strings, within 3, hanging 3.

steps.title: רב פפא rules on the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that the הלכה is four strings, attached within three fingerbreadths of the edge, hanging down four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says the הלכה is: four strings, placed within three fingerbreadths of the edge, hanging down four.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא decides the practical law. He mixes the two opinions from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא takes four strings and a hanging length of four from רב הונא. He takes the distance from the edge, within three, from רב יהודה. So the הלכה is a combination, not a full win for either side.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law, the final ruling

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling is four strings, placed within three fingerbreadths of the edge, hanging four fingerbreadths.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical measurements for making ציצית, and it is the ruling the next step challenges.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says: the halakha is:
four strings within three fingerbreadths,
hanging down four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רב הונא and רב יהודה by combining parts of each.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הלכה: four strings, within three fingerbreadths of the edge, hanging four.

steps.title: But ציצית have no fixed measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether ציצית really have a measure, and contradicts this with a ברייתא saying the elders of both schools agreed that ציצית have no measure, just like a לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean ציצית have a set measure? But a ברייתא says: "ציצית" means only something that sticks out, of any length. The elders of בית שמאי and בית הלל once went up to the attic of יוחנן בן בתירא and said: ציצית have no measure, and similarly a לולב has no measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges everything said so far. All these numbers suggest ציצית have a required size, but a ברייתא says they have no measure at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 16 to 19 all give exact lengths. The ברייתא learns from the word ציצית that any length is enough, and it reports that both schools agreed on this. That clashes with בית שמאי and בית הלל disagreeing about four or three fingerbreadths.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? Used to bring out an implication before challenging it
And contradict them, used to set one source against another
A required measure or size
Any amount at all, even the smallest
The palm branch taken on סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is against having ציצית strings. It agrees that strings are needed. It only says there is no required length.

phrases.english: Is this to say that they have a measure?
And contradict them: "Strings"
ציצית means nothing other than what sticks out,
and ציצית means only something of any length.
And the elders of Beit Shammai once went up

phrases.aramaic: וְזִקְנֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל לַעֲלִיַּית יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּתִירָא,
phrases.english: with the elders of Beit Hillel to the attic of Yochanan ben Beteira,
and they said: ציצית have no measure;

phrases.aramaic: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ, לוּלָב אֵין בּוֹ שִׁיעוּר.
phrases.english: similarly, a lulav has no measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea, assumed in steps 16 to 19, that ציצית have a required length.
steps.kashyaTarget: The measurements given for ציצית by the ברייתא, רב הונא, רב יהודה and רב פפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says the elders of both schools agreed that ציצית have no measure at all, so how can there be required lengths, and how can the two schools disagree about them?

steps.title: Does 'no measure' mean no measure at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge. It reads the ברייתא as saying ציצית have no required size whatsoever.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this mean ציצית have no measure at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge from step 20. It asks: doesn't 'ציצית have no measure' mean there is no size requirement at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא means there is no measure at all, it clashes with the exact sizes given in steps 16–19. The phrase 'מאי לאו' offers the simplest reading of the ברייתא so the contradiction stands out clearly. The word 'כלל' (at all) is what makes it a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Doesn't it mean...?' The גמרא suggests the obvious reading of a source in order to challenge something.
A required measure or size
At all, whatsoever

phrases.english: What, does it not mean
that it has no measure at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו אֵין לָהּ שִׁיעוּר כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It finishes the challenge from step 20 by stating the reading of the ברייתא that creates the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings in steps 16–19 that give ציצית exact sizes, ending with רב פפא's הלכה of four strings, attached within three fingerbreadths of the edge, hanging four.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא means ציצית have no measure at all, then any size requirement contradicts it.

steps.title: No, that is not what it means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer by rejecting the idea that 'no measure' means no measure at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge by saying 'No', meaning the ברייתא does not mean 'no measure at all.' This line only sets up the answer. The actual explanation comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one word, the גמרא rejects the reading that caused the contradiction. It will still need to explain what 'no measure' does mean, so that the ברייתא and the measurements can both be true. For now, only the rejection is in place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No.' This opens an answer that rejects the suggested reading.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the matter is settled here. The 'No' only says the challenge read the ברייתא wrongly. What 'no measure' really means is explained right after this.

phrases.english: No,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It begins to answer the challenge from step 21 by rejecting its reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenger's reading of the source (the full explanation follows in the next lines).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'ציצית have no measure' means there is no size requirement at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא does not mean 'no measure at all.' The exact meaning is given in the next lines.
